title: Patch rollback trace and evidence handoff - triage notes
content:
Purpose:
This working note documents a proposed operational workflow for capturing, preserving, and handing off forensic evidence when a patch rollout is rolled back. Focus areas: making scanner outputs (SBOMs and vuln reports) traceable to specific patch artifacts; ensuring RBAC v2 enforces minimal elevated access for evidence retrieval; audit-log schema adjustments to capture rollback tracepoints; and a SIEM ingest mapping to enable automated evidence collection and alerting.

Background:
- We've had two recent incidents where rollbacks occurred as part of emergency remediation and post-mortem evidence collection was inconsistent.
- Existing vulnerability pipeline: OSS scanner -> triage board (SEC-TRIAGE) -> patch PR -> deployment. Evidence artifacts are scattered across scanner exports, CI build artifacts, deploy logs and ticket threads.
- Current gaps: lack of stable linkage between scanner result id and build artifact SHA, insufficient audit entries that record who triggered a rollback and why, and unclear playbook for transferring evidence to compliance teams.

Objectives for this doc:
1) Define a minimal evidence model that ties a vuln finding to the patch (PR & build) and the rollback action.
2) Propose lightweight audit-log additions (schema) to capture rollback metadata and evidence pointers.
3) Lay out RBAC v2 role bindings required for evidence retrieval and automated collectors.
4) Map SIEM export fields so SOC can correlate rollback events with scanner signals and detection telemetry.
5) Draft an automated handoff flow that creates an immutable evidence bundle and notifies relevant owners.

Key definitions (working):
- finding_id: stable id from scanner run (UUID prefixed by scanner name).
- patch_artifact: container image or build artifact with digest and build metadata (git sha, pipeline id).
- rollback_action_id: generated id for the rollback operation (timestamped).
- evidence_bundle: tarball/immutable object containing scanner export, build manifest, deploy logs, canary metrics, and a signed note from the operator.

Findings from quick review of recent incidents:
- In 2 of 3 cases, the scanner's finding_id was not recorded in the PR description or CI metadata, making correlating later difficult.
- Rollbacks were triggered via two different UIs (console vs deployment-api) and only one produced an audit log entry with sufficient context.
- Evidence handoff was ad-hoc: engineers attached files to ticket threads rather than uploading to the compliance evidence store.

Proposed evidence model (minimal fields to capture):
- evidence_bundle_id (string)
- finding_id (string)
- patch_pr (url)
- artifact_digest (sha256)
- build_pipeline_id (string)
- deploy_target (cluster/region)
- operator (user id)
- rollback_action_id (string)
- rollback_reason (short text)
- timestamps: scanner_run, build_complete, deploy_start, rollback_initiated, bundle_created
- storage_pointer (S3/GS path + object version)

Audit log schema additions (append-only fields we suggest):
- event_type: string (e.g., "patch.deploy", "patch.rollback", "evidence.bundle.created")
- event_id: unique id
- related_ids: list of strings (finding_id, patch_pr, rollback_action_id) serialized as CSV in the log entry for SIEM-friendly ingestion
- operator: user/email
- actor_roles: comma separated roles at time of event (mapped to RBAC v2 token)
- actor_permissions_snapshot: short hash/reference to permissions snapshot if elevated actions were used
- outcome: success | failed | partial
- metadata: freeform key=val pairs for extra pointers (artifact_digest=..., storage_pointer=...)
notes:
RBAC v2 implications:
- Create a narrow role: evidence-reader which allows read-only access to evidence storage and read-only access to audit logs. This role should not grant deploy privileges.
- Create an evidence-bundler service account which can: read scanner exports, read build metadata, assemble evidence_bundle and write to immutable storage. This account should be audited and require short-lived credentials.

SIEM export mapping (field -> target index field):
- event_type -> redwood.event.type
- event_id -> redwood.event.id
- finding_id -> redwood.vuln.finding_id
- artifact_digest -> redwood.artifact.digest
- operator -> redwood.user.email
- rollback_reason -> redwood.rollback.reason
- storage_pointer -> redwood.evidence.location
- timestamps -> redwood.event.timestamps (store as ISO8601)
- related_ids -> redwood.related.ids (tokenized)

Automation hooks (simple end-to-end flow):
1) Scanner finishes and posts finding with finding_id to triage board (webhook).
2) When a patch PR is opened, CI must write "finding_id:<id>" into build metadata and PR body (automation template).
3) On deploy, deployment API emits event patch.deploy with event_id and artifact_digest.
4) If rollback is triggered, deployment API emits patch.rollback with rollback_action_id and references to event_id and finding_id when available.
5) Evidence-bundler listens for patch.rollback and patch.deploy events. If rollback_event has finding_id, bundler collects scanner export (by finding_id), build manifest (by artifact_digest), and deploy logs (by event_id). Bundler stores an immutable bundle and emits evidence.bundle.created event with storage_pointer.
6) SIEM ingests the three events (deploy, rollback, evidence.bundle) and correlates based on related_ids.
7) Compliance mailbox + ticket updated automatically with storage_pointer and short summary.

SLA and timing expectations (proposal):
- Evidence bundle creation: within 30 minutes of rollback_action (SLO).
- Audit log availability: logs should be queryable in SIEM within 2 minutes of event emission.
- Patch triage assignment: critical findings assigned within 1 business hour, high within 4 business hours.
- Evidence retention: 1 year for regular incidents, 7 years for incidents with PII/regulatory scope (subject to compliance approval).

Operational runbook (short):
- On rollback alert: assign incident owner (SEC oncall) -> confirm rollback_action_id -> verify evidence_bundle exists -> if missing, trigger ad-hoc bundler run with operator permission (RBAC-evidence-bundler only) -> upload bundle to compliance store -> attach storage pointer to incident ticket -> close with post-mortem template.

Edge cases and open questions:
- Unlinked scanner runs (finding_id missing): fallback process to reconstruct mapping via artifact timestamps and fuzzy matching of file hashes. Needs acceptance criteria and false-positive rate cap.
- Cross-account artifacts where artifact storage is in a different cloud account: ensure bundler has cross-account read role or secondary ingestion path.
- How to sign evidence bundles to prove chain-of-custody? Proposal: short-lived signing key minted per-bundler-run, signed manifest included in bundle. Key rotation and audit tracked by RBAC v2.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- (Aisha) Draft small PR to CI templates to inject finding_id into build metadata (ETA: 2026-06-25).
- (Diego) Prototype evidence-bundler lambda and storage layout (ETA: 2026-07-02).
- (Priya) Add audit-log schema changes to logging pipeline and SIEM mapping doc (ETA: 2026-06-28).
- (Liam) Draft RBAC v2 role grant matrix for evidence-reader and bundler (ETA: 2026-06-30).
- (Nina) Update compliance evidence retention policy draft to reflect new bundle lifecycle (ETA: 2026-07-05).

References and related tickets:
- JIRA SEC-4231 (incident triage #4231)
- Confluence: rbac-v2-design (design doc)
- GH PR: org/repo/pull/2345 (patch for vuln scanner integration)
- Internal SIEM connector guide: https://docs.siem.internal/connectors/redwood

- Sync with triage, deploy and compliance leads on 2026-06-22 to walk through bundler prototype and identify storage permissions.
